summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 58 (`ipns-signature-verify-coverage`) of the CipherBox project using the GSD workflow — adding IPNS signature verification coverage across Rust (`crates/core`, `crates/fuse`) and TypeScript (`sdk-core`, `web`) via a 4-plan, 2-wave TDD execution.
summary.outcome: All 4 plans executed and verified: cargo tests (core 75, fuse 87), apps/api jest (913/913), and SDK E2E (89/89) all passing; VERIFICATION.md written with `status: passed` (7/7 must-haves, D-01..D-13 confirmed in code); advisory code review findings queued for application.

repo: `crates/crypto` cannot dev-depend on `api-client/core` due to dependency cycles — shared Rust test vectors must live in `crates/fuse/tests/`, not `crates/crypto/tests/`
The D-09 tightening change-class (non-CAS embedded-sequence enforcement) historically broke 48/89 SDK E2E tests — treat any upsertFolderIpns changes as high-risk

API `.env` uses `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-ci-only` but SDK E2E harness defaults `SDK_E2E_SECRET` to `e2e-test-secret-do-not-use-in-production` — these must be aligned before running the E2E suite locally
The `expectedSequenceNumber` guard at the CAS 409 conflict path is intentional and must not be removed during D-09 enforcement work
`commit_failed` from the GSD commit helper is a known false-negative — always verify with `git log` rather than retrying the commit
RESEARCH.md `## Open Questions` sections must be annotated with `(RESOLVED)` markers or the plan-checker emits a cosmetic warning that blocks clean verification

code.finding: `ciborium` dependency is present here — a mid-execution diagnostic falsely reported it missing, likely reading a stale pre-commit view
Uses unchecked `seq + 1` arithmetic; crate convention is `checked_add` — flagged as WR-01 in code review and queued for fix

workflow: Sequential execution on the feature branch is safer than parallel worktrees for security/crypto phases — avoids cwd-drift, merge conflicts, and stranded worktree cleanup

Executor subagents can overflow into subsequent plans in the same run (58-02 agent also completed 58-03) — always verify which plans actually executed by reading git log, not just the agent's return value

When an executor agent crashes mid-plan due to a socket error, partial work (including uncommitted diffs) survives on disk — assess actual disk+git state before spawning a continuation to avoid re-doing committed tasks
Phase verifier and code reviewer are fully independent and should always be spawned in parallel to save wall-clock time
SDK E2E test-login endpoint returns 400 (not 401) for wrong payload shape, making secret-mismatch diagnosis non-obvious — probe payload shape from the harness source before assuming a secret issue

friction: 58-01 executor crashed mid-execution (API socket error / connection closed) with Task 3 done but uncommitted and Task 4 not started — required a manual continuation agent
58-02 executor skipped the full SDK E2E gate (labeled 'infra-limited') due to TEST_LOGIN_SECRET mismatch, requiring a separate focused agent to run the gate post-hoc
58-02 executor overflowed into 58-03 without being instructed to — created plan-tracking confusion and required auditing git log to determine actual state
`commit_failed` false-negative from the GSD commit helper caused unnecessary alarm and investigation before `git log` confirmed the commit landed
test-login endpoint returned 400 rather than 401 when probed with wrong payload shape, obscuring whether the secret or the request format was the issue
open_items: 4 code review findings (including WR-01: unchecked `seq + 1` in `replay.rs`) were queued for a code-fixer agent — transcript ends before confirming the fixes landed and suites re-passed

TEST_LOGIN_SECRET / SDK_E2E_SECRET env mismatch between API `.env` and SDK E2E harness should be permanently resolved (e.g., via a shared `.env.test` or documented alignment step) to prevent future E2E gate failures
